# @zakkster/lite-arena

> Zero-GC Entity-Component-System (ECS) memory allocator in ~280 lines.
> Generational handles defeat ABA; SoA sparse sets give cache-friendly
> iteration; swap-and-pop keeps removal O(1) without array shifts.

Use this library when you need to manage 1,000-100,000 game entities with
multiple components per entity, at 60 fps, without GC pauses. It's a primitive,
not a framework: no query language, no scene graph, no rendering. Drop it
into a custom game loop, particle system, simulation, or canvas overlay.

The library exports two classes: `Arena` (the universe) and `SparseSet` (one
per component). All memory is pre-allocated at construction.

## API surface

```ts
import { Arena, SparseSet, Entity } from '@zakkster/lite-arena';

// Construction (once, at startup):
const arena = new Arena(maxEntities: number);   // [1, 1_048_575]
// Optional dev-only assertions (OFF and zero-cost in production):
//   new Arena(maxEntities, { checked: true });  // stale join()/misused idx() throw

// Components: SoA schemas mapped to parallel TypedArrays.
const Pos = arena.registerComponent({
  x: Float32Array,
  y: Float32Array,
});

// Optional: back a component's payload with buffers YOU own (ArrayBuffer or
// SharedArrayBuffer) so it can be shared with a Worker. One buffer per field,
// each exactly capacity * BYTES_PER_ELEMENT bytes; validated fail-closed both
// ways. Omit to own-allocate (byte-identical to before). reserve() refuses to
// grow an arena that has any caller-backed component.
const sab = new SharedArrayBuffer(arena.capacity * Float32Array.BYTES_PER_ELEMENT);
const Vel = arena.registerComponent({ vx: Float32Array }, { buffers: { vx: sab } });

// Optional: OFFLOAD a component's payload to a Worker with a zero-copy
// transferable-ArrayBuffer round-trip. Works INSIDE a Twitch extension iframe --
// no SharedArrayBuffer, no cross-origin isolation, no atomics. detach() collects
// the backing buffer for the postMessage transfer list; transferring it detaches
// the view; rebind() re-adopts the buffer the Worker transfers back (validated
// fail-closed); isDetached() is a once-per-frame guard, never per element.
const [vxBuf] = Vel.detach(['vx']);          // send leg: transfer vxBuf (list [vxBuf])
// ...worker transforms vxBuf in place and transfers it back...
if (Vel.isDetached('vx')) { /* skip systems reading vx until it returns */ }
Vel.rebind({ vx: vxBuf });                   // return leg: Vel.data.vx is live again

// Entity lifecycle:
const e: Entity = arena.spawn();        // O(1), throws when full (throw names full vs retired)
arena.isAlive(e): boolean;              // O(1), safe on arbitrary input
arena.despawn(e): boolean;              // O(1), cascades to every component
arena.remainingCapacity(): number;      // O(1), = capacity - activeCount - retiredCount
arena.clear();                          // reset in place (no realloc); ALL prior handles die

// Component ops on SparseSet<T>:
Pos.add(e): number;        // returns dense index, or -1 if dead
Pos.has(e): boolean;       // O(1), validates liveness + membership
Pos.remove(e): boolean;    // O(1) swap-and-pop
Pos.idx(e): number;        // UNSAFE fast-path — no checks; use only after has()

// Tag components (zero-size membership markers):
const Frozen = arena.registerTag();     // SparseSet, empty null-proto data
Frozen.add(e); Frozen.has(e); Frozen.remove(e);   // dense/count as usual

// Two-component join (rarest-first). Cold planner; caller writes the loop.
const j = arena.join(Pos, Frozen);      // driver = the smaller-count set
const drv = j.driver, oth = j.other, n = j.count;   // hoist, then loop:
for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
  const e = drv.dense[i];
  if (!oth.has(e)) continue;            // e has BOTH components
  // ...
}

// Hot loop (the canonical pattern):
const n = Pos.count;
const x = Pos.data.x;       // hoist the typed-array ref
const y = Pos.data.y;
for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
  x[i] += vx[i] * dt;
  y[i] += vy[i] * dt;
}

// Capacity growth (cold, between-frames, EXPLICIT only):
arena.reserve(newCap): boolean;   // grows the universe; false if newCap <= cap
// spawn() at capacity THROWS -- it never auto-grows. Call reserve() yourself
// between frames. It reallocates every backing array, so any ref you hoisted
// (const x = Pos.data.x) is STALE afterward -- re-read Pos.data.x post-reserve.
```

## Key invariants

- `dense[0..count)` is always contiguous and packed. Iterate it directly.
- Indices `[count, capacity)` in `dense` and `data.*` are stale; don't read them.
- Handle layout is opaque. Never decompose entity handles by hand.
- `Generation = 0` is reserved as "never alive"; synthesizing handle `0` is
  guaranteed to be rejected on a fresh arena.
- Generational rollover is fail-closed: a slot that exhausts its 4095 live
  generations is permanently retired on despawn (never recycled), so a stale
  handle can never alias as valid. `arena.retiredCount` counts retired slots;
  it stays `0` on realistic workloads. See decisions/0001-generational-rollover.md.
- Conservation law: every slot is live, free, or retired, so
  `activeCount + retiredCount + remainingCapacity() === capacity` holds after
  every operation. `remainingCapacity()` (O(1)) is the free count; it drops below
  `capacity - activeCount` once slots retire, and `spawn()`'s exhaustion throw
  reports all three counts and names whether the arena is full or retirement-shrunk
  (so an empty-but-exhausted arena does not read as a phantom leak).
- `clear()` resets the arena to empty WITHOUT reallocating (rebuilds the free
  list, bumps every generation, revives retired slots, zeroes each component's
  count); it is O(capacity) and allocates nothing. Every handle minted before
  `clear()` is invalid afterward -- the honest contract of a reset. Retirement is
  observed via the counter, never a callback: there is deliberately no `onRetire`
  (see decisions/0004-retirement-observability-and-clear.md).
- Checked mode (`new Arena(n, { checked: true })`) is OFF by default and zero-cost
  in production. When on: reading a `join()` plan after a later `join()` throws,
  and `idx()` on a dead/non-member entity throws. The checked `idx` shadows the
  prototype method as an own property, so the production `idx()` fast path is
  byte-for-byte unchanged.
- `idx()` skips validation; only call inside loops where validity is guaranteed.
- `despawn()` automatically removes the entity from every registered component.
- `registerComponent(schema)` validates the schema at registration (a cold path):
  every field type must be one of the nine numeric TypedArray constructors
  (Int8/Uint8/Uint8Clamped/Int16/Uint16/Int32/Uint32/Float32/Float64Array), or
  it throws a library error naming the key. `Array`, `Object`, `SharedArrayBuffer`,
  `BigInt64Array`, a string, `null`, etc. are all rejected -- a schema that lies
  about its types never silently produces a polymorphic Array or a boxed Number.
- `comp.data` is an `Object.create(null)` bag, not a plain `{}`: it has the
  schema's keys and NO prototype, so `toString` / `constructor` are usable field
  names and a `__proto__` schema key fails closed instead of dropping a field.
- `registerTag()` is `registerComponent({})`: membership only; `data` is an empty
  null-prototype object (`Object.keys(data).length === 0`).
- `SparseSet` is exported, but constructing one directly requires the owning
  `Arena` and a capacity equal to `arena.capacity`; a mismatch throws. Prefer
  `arena.registerComponent(schema)`, which always constructs it correctly.
- `join(a, b)` returns a REUSED scratch `{driver, other, count}` (driver = the
  smaller-count set); it allocates nothing and is called once per system, cold.
  It is a planner, not an iterator -- there is deliberately no `query()` or
  `forEach()`. Consume the result before the next `join()` on the same arena.
- The arena NEVER auto-grows. `spawn()` at capacity throws; growth happens only
  through an explicit, between-frames `reserve(newCap)`. `reserve()` reallocates
  every backing buffer (copying live contents; all handles/memberships/dense
  indices preserved), so hoisted refs like `const x = comp.data.x` are stale
  after it returns -- re-read them. Grow-only: `newCap <= capacity` is a no-op.
- Caller-supplied buffers (`registerComponent(schema, { buffers })`): each
  `data[key]` can VIEW a buffer the caller owns -- an `ArrayBuffer` or
  `SharedArrayBuffer` of exactly `capacity * BYTES_PER_ELEMENT` bytes -- so a
  component's payload can live in memory shared with a Worker. Validated
  fail-closed both ways: every declared field needs a correctly-typed,
  correctly-sized buffer, and no buffer may target an undeclared field; a
  missing/null buffer for a declared field throws rather than silently
  own-allocating. Only `data.*` is shareable -- `count` and `dense` are NOT
  shared, so a Worker can read/write `data.*` over a range the main thread hands
  it by message (postMessage is the fence) but CANNOT iterate the set itself yet.
  No atomics, no locking, no multi-writer. The arena never frees, grows, or
  reassigns a caller-supplied buffer, and `reserve()` throws if any component is
  caller-backed. See decisions/0006-caller-supplied-buffers.md.
- Transferable round-trip (`detach` / `rebind` / `isDetached`): OFFLOAD a
  component's payload to a Worker with zero copy, using a plain `ArrayBuffer` and
  `postMessage(buf, [buf])` -- no `SharedArrayBuffer`, so it runs INSIDE a Twitch
  extension iframe (which cannot be cross-origin isolated). `detach(keys?)`
  collects the backing buffer(s) for the transfer list; transferring one detaches
  the sender's view (`byteLength` 0). `rebind(buffers)` re-adopts the buffer(s) a
  Worker transfers back -- a PARTIAL, fail-closed map (unknown key, wrong type, or
  wrong size throws; nothing is re-pointed until every buffer passes), after which
  the set is caller-backed. `isDetached(key)` is truthful (`byteLength === 0`) and
  is the sanctioned ONCE-PER-FRAME system guard -- raw `data[key][i]` reads are
  not policed (they cannot be, without taxing the hot path), so a hot loop over a
  detached field is a caller bug. `reserve()` also refuses a component with a
  detached field. The transfer is the fence: the buffer is owned by exactly one
  thread at a time. See decisions/0007-transferable-roundtrip.md.

## Files

- [README.md](README.md): Full documentation, benchmarks, mermaid diagrams,
  FAQ, edge cases. Start here.
- [./Arena.js](./Arena.js): The implementation (~280 lines, MIT, ESM).
- [./Arena.d.ts](./Arena.d.ts): TypeScript definitions, fully typed including
  `ComponentData<T>` generic for typed `data` field access.
- [test/Arena.test.js](test/Arena.test.js): node:test unit suite including a
  randomized churn oracle, tag/join stress, a reserve() growth oracle,
  retirement/`clear()` observability, checked-mode assertions, caller-supplied
  buffer validation (both directions), and a zero-allocation guarantee under
  `--expose-gc`.
- [test/cross-thread.test.js](test/cross-thread.test.js): a `worker_threads`
  smoke test proving a SharedArrayBuffer-backed component payload is reachable
  from a Worker both ways, postMessage-fenced.
- [test/transfer.test.js](test/transfer.test.js): a `worker_threads` test proving
  the transferable-`ArrayBuffer` round-trip (detach -> transfer -> transform ->
  transfer back -> rebind) across a real thread boundary, twice; plain
  `ArrayBuffer`, no cross-origin isolation.
- [bench/bench.js](bench/bench.js): Benchmark harness comparing against
  `Map<id, object>`, `Array<Object>`, and a no-ECS manual SoA.
- [demo/demo.html](demo/demo.html): 50,000-particle gravity-well demo,
  toggleable backend, live FPS / heap stats. One backend, "lite-arena + Worker",
  runs the physics off-thread via the 1.8.0 transferable round-trip
  ([demo/worker.js](demo/worker.js)): detach -> transfer -> integrate -> transfer
  back -> rebind, plain `ArrayBuffer`, no cross-origin isolation. Module workers
  do not load over `file://`, so that backend needs a plain static server (no
  COOP/COEP headers); the other three backends run straight from `file://`.

## Headline performance

On a 2022 laptop, iteration of 10,000 entities × 200 frames (illustrative --
ratios are the portable result; see README for v1.6.1 numbers on current hardware):

| Strategy | ms | vs lite-arena |
|---|---:|---:|
| **lite-arena**     | **8.5 ms** | **1.00×** |
| Manual SoA (no ECS) | 9.2 ms | 1.09× |
| Array<Object>       | 28.6 ms | 3.38× |
| Map<id, object>     | 39.2 ms | 4.63× |

Heap delta across all backends: < 100 bytes. The headline win is **iteration
speed**, not spawn throughput; if your bottleneck is per-frame spawn churn,
benchmark first — a bare TypedArray pool may suffice.

## When NOT to use this

- You have <500 entities. The JIT already inlines your class-based code fine.
- You need complex archetype queries ("entities with A and B but not C, sorted
  by D"). Use [bitecs](https://github.com/NateTheGreatt/bitECS) or similar.
- Your components store arbitrary JS objects, not numbers. SoA is for
  primitive numeric fields; if you need a `name: string` field, store the
  string in a parallel `string[]` outside the ECS and use the entity index
  as a key.

## Sibling packages

Part of the `@zakkster/*` zero-GC ecosystem:

- `@zakkster/lite-signal` — reactive graph (873 lines, 78 tests)
- `@zakkster/lite-scheduler` — frame budget manager with priority lanes
- `@zakkster/lite-batch-buffer` — pre-allocated WebGL vertex buffer

All three are designed to compose: the scheduler drives the frame, lite-arena
manages entity state, lite-batch-buffer streams vertices to the GPU. Together
they fit comfortably in Twitch's 1 MB / 3 s extension budget.
